es.summary: Estado en el que el cuerpo no recibe suficientes calorías, proteínas o micronutrientes para mantener la salud. Puede ser por ingesta insuficiente, mala absorción o aumento de requerimientos.
key_points: Incluye desnutrición proteico‑energética (kwashiorkor, marasmo) y desequilibrios de micronutrientes
Factores de riesgo: edad extrema, enfermedades crónicas, pobreza y dietas restrictivas
Marcadores de laboratorio: albúmina <3.5 g/dL, prealbúmina <18 mg/dL, IMC <18.5 kg/m²
Intervención principal: re‑alimentación gradual y suplementación de micronutrientes

pathophysiology: Ingesta calórica/proteica < requerimientos → déficit de energía y síntesis de proteínas
Disminución de albúmina y prealbúmina por falta de aminoácidos
Pérdida de masa muscular y tejido subcutáneo
Alteración de la respuesta inmune por déficit de vitaminas y minerales
risk_factors: Dietas restrictivas o trastornos de la alimentación
Infecciones prolongadas con fiebre y diarrea
signs_symptoms: IMC <18.5 kg/m² o <5 percentil en niños
Cambios en la piel y cabello (descamación, cabello quebradizo)
diagnostics: Historia dietética y examen físico completo
Peso, talla, IMC, % de grasa corporal
Laboratorio: albúmina, prealbúmina, hemoglobina, electrolitos, vitaminas (A, D, B12)
Radiografía de tórax si se sospecha edema pulmonar
treatment: Re‑alimentación oral con dietas hipercalóricas y altas en proteína
Suplementos de vitaminas y minerales según déficit
Nutrición enteral si la ingesta oral es insuficiente
Nutrición parenteral en casos graves o intolerancia gastrointestinal
Monitoreo de peso y laboratorios cada 1‑2 semanas
complications: Retraso del crecimiento y desarrollo en niños
nursing_care: Valoración de peso, talla, IMC y signos de edema diariamente
Monitorizar albúmina y electrolitos cada 48‑72 h
Registrar ingesta calórica y de líquidos
Posicionar al paciente en decúbito supino o semi‑Fowler según tolerancia
Priorizar la seguridad de la vía de alimentación (NG, PEG)
patient_teaching: Enseñar la importancia de comidas frecuentes y densas en energía
Demostrar cómo leer etiquetas para identificar fuentes de proteína y vitaminas
Instruir sobre signos de deshidratación y cuándo buscar ayuda médica
Fomentar la participación de la familia en la preparación de alimentos nutritivos

care_plans.diagnosis: Desequilibrio nutricional: inferior a las necesidades corporales
related_to: ingesta insuficiente de calorías y proteínas
enfermedad crónica con aumento de requerimientos
pobreza y falta de acceso a alimentos nutritivos
outcomes: Estado nutricional: peso corporal dentro del 5 % del objetivo en 4 semanas
Consumo de proteínas: ≥1.2 g/kg/día en 2 semanas
Nivel de albúmina: ≥3.5 g/dL en 3 semanas

interventions.action: Realizar valoración nutricional completa y registrar ingesta calórica diaria
interventions.rationale: Permite identificar déficit y planificar la re‑alimentación

interventions.action: Ofrecer dieta hipercalórica y alta en proteína en pequeñas porciones frecuentes
interventions.rationale: Facilita la tolerancia y aumenta la ingesta total

interventions.action: Administrar suplementos de vitaminas y minerales según resultados de laboratorio
interventions.rationale: Corrige deficiencias específicas y previene complicaciones

interventions.action: Monitorear peso y parámetros de laboratorio (albúmina, prealbúmina) cada 48 h
interventions.rationale: Evalúa la respuesta al tratamiento y permite ajustes oportunos

interventions.action: Educar al paciente y familia sobre preparación de alimentos ricos en energía y proteína
interventions.rationale: Promueve la adherencia y la autosuficiencia nutricional

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de déficit de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: Hidratación: ingesta de líquidos ≥30 mL/kg/día en 48 h
Signos de deshidratación: ausentes en evaluación diaria

interventions.action: Evaluar balance hídrico cada turno (entrada vs salida)
interventions.rationale: Detecta temprano déficit de líquidos

interventions.action: Ofrecer líquidos claros y soluciones de rehidratación oral cada 2 h
interventions.rationale: Reemplaza pérdidas y previene deshidratación

interventions.action: Monitorizar presión arterial, frecuencia cardíaca y turgencia cutánea
interventions.rationale: Identifica signos fisiológicos de hipovolemia

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de beber al menos 2 L de agua al día
interventions.rationale: Fomenta la autosuficiencia en la hidratación

interventions.action: Notificar al médico si el balance hídrico es negativo >‑500 mL/24 h
interventions.rationale: Permite intervención médica o terapia intravenosa temprana

en.summary: A state in which the body does not receive enough calories, protein, or micronutrients to maintain health. It can result from inadequate intake, poor absorption, or increased requirements.
key_points: Includes protein-energy malnutrition (kwashiorkor, marasmus) and micronutrient imbalances
Risk factors: extreme age, chronic diseases, poverty, restrictive diets
Laboratory markers: albumin <3.5 g/dL, prealbumin <18 mg/dL, BMI <18.5 kg/m²
Primary intervention: gradual refeeding and micronutrient supplementation

pathophysiology: Caloric/protein intake < requirements → energy deficit and impaired protein synthesis
Reduced albumin and prealbumin due to amino acid deficiency
Loss of muscle mass and subcutaneous tissue
Immune response altered by vitamin and mineral deficits
risk_factors: Prolonged infections with fever and diarrhea
signs_symptoms: BMI <18.5 kg/m² or <5th percentile in children
Skin and hair changes (desquamation, brittle hair)
diagnostics: Dietary history and comprehensive physical exam
Laboratory: albumin, prealbumin, hemoglobin, electrolytes, vitamins (A, D, B12)
Chest X‑ray if pulmonary edema suspected
treatment: Oral refeeding with hypercaloric, high‑protein diets
Vitamin and mineral supplements per deficits
Enteral nutrition if oral intake insufficient
Parenteral nutrition in severe cases or GI intolerance
Monitor weight and labs every 1–2 weeks
complications: Growth and developmental delay in children
nursing_care: Assess weight, height, BMI, and edema signs daily
Monitor albumin and electrolytes every 48–72 h
Position patient supine or semi‑Fowler as tolerated
patient_teaching: Teach importance of frequent, energy‑dense meals
Show how to read labels for protein and vitamin sources
Explain dehydration signs and when to seek medical help
Encourage family involvement in preparing nutritious foods

care_plans.diagnosis: Imbalanced nutrition: less than body requirements
related_to: poverty and lack of access to nutritious foods
outcomes: Nutritional status: body weight within 5 % of goal in 4 weeks

interventions.action: Perform comprehensive nutritional assessment and record daily caloric intake
interventions.rationale: Identifies deficits and plans refeeding

interventions.action: Offer hypercaloric, high‑protein diet in small, frequent portions
interventions.rationale: Improves tolerance and increases total intake

interventions.action: Administer vitamin and mineral supplements per lab results
interventions.rationale: Corrects specific deficiencies and prevents complications

interventions.action: Monitor weight and laboratory parameters (albumin, prealbumin) every 48 h
interventions.rationale: Evaluates treatment response and allows timely adjustments

interventions.action: Educate patient and family on preparing energy‑rich, protein‑dense foods
interventions.rationale: Promotes adherence and nutritional self‑sufficiency

outcomes: Hydration: fluid intake ≥30 mL/kg/day in 48 h
Dehydration signs: absent on daily assessment

interventions.action: Assess fluid balance each shift (input vs output)
interventions.rationale: Detects early fluid deficit

interventions.action: Offer clear fluids and oral rehydration solutions every 2 h
interventions.rationale: Replaces losses and prevents dehydration

interventions.action: Monitor blood pressure, heart rate, and skin turgor
interventions.rationale: Identifies physiological signs of hypovolemia

interventions.action: Educate patient on importance of drinking at least 2 L of water daily
interventions.rationale: Encourages self‑hydration

interventions.action: Notify physician if fluid balance is negative >‑500 mL/24 h
interventions.rationale: Allows early medical intervention or IV therapy

summary.0.quote: Malnutrition means that your body isn't getting enough calories or the right balance of nutrients to stay healthy.

key_points.0.quote: Two serious forms of this are kwashiorkor and marasmus.

sections.pathophysiology.3.quote: Healing is compromised when nutritional deficits are present, preventing immune-modulating cells from functioning properly.

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: Low calorie intake is a common cause of undernutrition and is commonly associated with poverty, homelessness, mental disorders, and cognitive disorders.

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: Infections, inflammatory disease, metabolic conditions, and eating disorders are all medical conditions that have a direct effect on nutritional status.

sections.risk_factors.4.quote: Conditions associated with dehydration include vomiting, diarrhea, prolonged fevers, and excessive sweat due to heat stroke.

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: The symptoms of malnutrition can vary. You may have no symptoms, but if you do, they may include: Fatigue and weakness Dizziness Losing weight without trying Low body weight Slow growth or development in children Frequent infections or slow healing Dry skin or brittle hair and nails Swelling in the legs, feet, or belly How is malnutrition diagnosed?

sections.signs_symptoms.4.quote: You may have no symptoms, but if you do, they may include: Fatigue and weakness Dizziness Losing weight without trying Low body weight Slow growth or development in children Frequent infections or slow healing Dry skin or brittle hair and nails Swelling in the legs, feet, or belly How is malnutrition diagnosed?

sections.diagnostics.0.quote: A nutrition assessment includes subjective data, including demographic and sociocultural data, lifestyle cues, and medical history. It also includes objective data gathered from physical exams, labs, and diagnostic tests.

sections.diagnostics.1.quote: The measure of body mass index (BMI) is a commonly used tool that analyzes height and weight to provide a measurement relative to generalized standards.

sections.treatment.0.quote: Chronic infectious states often benefit from a high- calorie , high-protein diet to meet elevated energy demands.

sections.treatment.1.quote: Iron supplements, vitamin B12 injections, folate supplements, and increased iron or folate intake in the diet can help increase hemoglobin levels.

sections.complications.1.quote: You may have no symptoms, but if you do, they may include: Fatigue and weakness Dizziness Losing weight without trying Low body weight Slow growth or development in children Frequent infections or slow healing Dry skin or brittle hair and nails Swelling in the legs, feet, or belly How is malnutrition diagnosed?

sections.complications.3.quote: Without the right vitamins, your body cannot stay healthy and may develop specific diseases. For example, scurvy can develop from too little vitamin C , rickets from too little vitamin D , and anemia from too little iron or vitamin B12 .

sections.complications.4.quote: If a caloric deficit is prolonged and starvation ensues, the body will metabolize proteins, which can lead to life-threatening medical conditions and death.
